note: Incumbent map for Anti Fund's physical lanes: the unicorns, public companies and repeat government-funded players already putting down real infrastructure, so a seed fund knows where not to fight and can check whether a new startup goes head-on against them, supplies them, or is truly new. Same habits as entities.json: every identifier was checked by hand on 2026-10-08 (legal names and UEIs with gt.usaspending.awards() by name and then by UEI; NRC dockets with gt.nrc, checking who files on them; job slugs by fetching the board and reading the postings' own company description). Identifiers that could not be verified are left out, and rejected look-alikes are listed so nobody re-adds them. 'why_url' is the source for 'why'. Portfolio companies are never listed as incumbents.
gotchas: USAspending's recipient search also matches parent UEIs: awards(<parent UEI>) returns subsidiaries' awards with their own UEIs (Heron Systems under Shield AI, BlueHalo LLC under AeroVironment, SRCTEC under SRC, NAC International under Centrus). Dedupe by award id, and filter on Recipient UEI if you need one entity only.
USAspending name search matches substrings: 'NEROS' hits CISNEROS, 'ORANO' hits TORANOMON, 'X ENERGY' hits ATREX ENERGY, 'MATX' hits ASTHMATX, 'URENCO' hits EURENCO. Search by UEI.

Some incumbents' money sits under other names: TerraPower's $1.70B DOE award is under US SFR OWNER LLC, Forterra still contracts as ROBOTIC RESEARCH OPCO, LLC, Red Cat as TEAL DRONES INC, MP Materials as MP MINE OPERATIONS LLC.
nrc.docket('07003103') (Urenco USA) will raise: the docket holds 6,020 documents, above the 5,000-document guard in gt/nrc.py.

lanes.name: Tunneling and underground infrastructure

lanes.name: Brain-computer interfaces
lanes.description: Implanted and non-invasive neural interfaces that read from or write to the brain.

companies.name: Saildrone
companies.why: 60 federal prime awards ($72.5M) since 2015; the Coast Guard now buys maritime-domain-awareness coverage from its USV fleet ($15.6M Northeast and Great Lakes call order, Mar 2026).

companies.name: HavocAI
companies.why: Raised about $200M since 2024, most recently $100M (May 2026) with Lockheed Martin and SAIC investing, to build autonomous boats at volume.
companies.note: Now calls itself 'Havoc' in postings. Its federal record so far is two 2026 Army SBIR Phase II awards ($4.0M).

companies.name: BlackSea Technologies (AEVEX)
companies.why: Mass-produces the Navy's GARC drone boats at a former Baltimore shipyard; AEVEX agreed in Aug 2026 to buy it for up to $650M (closed Sept 2026).
companies.note: BlackSea has no prime awards of its own in USAspending ('BLACKSEA' and 'BLACK SEA TECHNOLOGIES' return nothing). The identifiers are the new parent's: AEVEX's $1.66B is mostly Air Force Big Safari ISR work, so expect non-maritime signals.

companies.name: Shield AI
companies.why: Shield AI Inc. has 407 FAA-registered aircraft (405 V-BATs and 2 X-BATs, newest Sept 29, 2026), the biggest fleet among these incumbents, plus $130M in federal prime awards led by Coast Guard V-BAT services.
companies.note: Martin UAV (original V-BAT maker; 6 more aircraft registered in its name) and Heron Systems are acquired units. Searching Shield AI's UEI also returns Heron's award.

companies.name: Skydio
companies.why: 176 federal prime awards since 2019 (136 since 2024) from many civil and defense buyers, e.g. X2D drones for Ukraine's border guard via the State Department (2022); the FAA lists it as maker of the X10, X2E and Skydio 2.

companies.name: AeroVironment (incl. BlueHalo)
companies.why: Maker of Switchblade, Puma and Raven with $7.3B in federal prime awards across its entities and BlueHalo (now part of AV, maker of the Titan counter-drone system), including a $406.5M Army Switchblade production contract (2020).
companies.note: USAspending files BlueHalo LLC (HE86H1JJJTK5) under AV's parent UEI MWKWXVSSC518, and Arcturus UAV under YJG1MDHLBC88, so searching a parent UEI returns the children too. Careers run on Workday, not a supported board.

companies.name: Red Cat (Teal Drones)
companies.why: Its Teal Black Widow beat Skydio to become the Army's Short Range Reconnaissance program of record (Nov 2024; about 5,880 systems planned over five years).
companies.note: Federal awards sit under subsidiary Teal Drones (49 awards, $6.4M); a 'RED CAT HOLDINGS' name search returns only Teal.

companies.name: Neros
companies.why: Holds an Army Purpose-Built Attritable System (PBAS) contract for small attritable drones; delivery order 1 was $17.5M (July 2026), and all 29 of its federal awards date from 2024 on.
rejected: SISNEROS BROS. MFG., LLC. (substring match on 'NEROS')

companies.name: Epirus
companies.why: Its Leonidas high-power microwave is the base of the Army's IFPC-HPM counter-swarm system: $66.1M for four prototypes, then a $43.5M Gen II order (July 2025); raised a $250M Series D in 2025.
companies.note: The Army HPM deals do not appear among its USAspending prime awards (14 awards, $4.6M).

companies.name: SRC, Inc.
companies.why: Radar and electronic-warfare house with $5.5B in federal prime awards under its UEIs (incl. manufacturing arm SRCTec); 26 award descriptions mention C-UAS, and it built the Army's DUKE V2 counter-IED jammers ($319.6M, 2009).
rejected: SRC INC (UEI UNFXSYKV4K19: Forest Service and CDC vendor, not under SRC's parent)
companies.note: Searching DC9UXK381JR5 also returns SRCTEC, LLC, SAZE TECHNOLOGIES, LLC and SYRACUSE RESEARCH CORP (SRC's old name) as children.

companies.name: DroneShield
companies.why: ASX-listed counter-drone maker; its US arm won a $13.8M Army C-sUAS award to equip four fixed-site zones (June 2026), part of $17.3M in US federal awards since 2024.

companies.name: Applied Intuition
companies.why: Valued at $15B by its own account; sells vehicle autonomy to defense as well as automotive, trucking, construction and mining customers, with Air Force, Army and Missile Defense Agency software awards.
companies.note: EPISYS SCIENCE INC (UEI U719HNLEESB3, 62 awards, $64.9M of autonomy work) is reported as an Applied acquisition but USAspending does not link it and no primary source confirmed it here, so it is left out.

companies.name: Forterra
companies.why: The renamed Robotic Research (Apr 2024): its autonomy drives Oshkosh vehicles in the Marine Corps' ROGUE-Fires ($92M Block 2 production order with Oshkosh, 2026), and it has 87 federal prime awards ($68.6M) under its old name.
companies.note: USAspending still lists the contracting entity under its old name (Clarksburg, MD; alternate names include ROBOTIC RESEARCH LLC), so a 'FORTERRA' search misses it.

companies.name: Overland AI
companies.why: Repeat off-road autonomy contractor: 9 Army, Navy and Marine Corps awards ($11.4M) since 2023, the latest an Army SBIR Phase II (Mar 2026).

companies.name: Castelion
companies.why: $261M in federal awards since 2023 for low-cost long-range strike weapons, led by a $155M Navy order (Feb 2026) and a $55.8M Air Force award (2024).

companies.name: X-Bow Systems
companies.why: Solid-rocket-motor maker with $182M in Air Force and Army awards, led by a $129.5M 'Advanced Integrated Motor Manufacturing' contract (Sept 2025).

companies.name: Zone 5 Technologies
companies.why: 19 Air Force and SOCOM awards ($29.4M), from AFRL's Golden Horde networked-weapons work (2021) to an SBIR Phase III called Rusty Dagger (June 2026).

companies.name: Ursa Major
companies.why: Rocket-engine and motor maker for hypersonics, missiles and launch: 16 federal awards ($43.5M), including a $20M Air Force storable hypersonic engine contract (May 2025).

companies.name: Hadrian
companies.why: Builds automated precision-machining factories (hiring in Los Angeles, Mesa AZ and Cherokee AL) and won a $39.2M Army award (Mar 2026).

companies.name: Divergent
companies.why: Additive-manufacturing supplier to defense primes, valued at $2.3B after a $290M Series E (Sept 2025), and opening a Long Beach factory for missile airframes.

companies.name: Machina Labs
companies.why: Robotic sheet-metal forming for the Air Force and NASA: 13 federal awards ($12.8M) since 2020, including Air Force incremental sheet forming (Feb 2025).

companies.name: Firestorm Labs
companies.why: The Air Force bought its container-sized xCell drone factory ($18.8M, Oct 2025); $53.8M in federal awards since 2023, 34 FAA-registered Tempest drones and a $47M Series A (2025).
rejected: firestormlabs.com (now redirects to an unrelated business, Shady Pets LLC)

companies.name: MP Materials
companies.why: The Pentagon became its largest shareholder ($400M preferred, July 2025), guarantees a $110/kg NdPr price floor, and has first call on every magnet from its planned 10X plant in Texas.
companies.note: The 2025 equity, price floor and offtake are not prime awards in USAspending; the visible awards are a DLA NdPr oxide buy ($11.0M, 2024) and a DPA Title III grant (2020).

companies.name: Vulcan Elements
companies.why: Lined up a $620M Pentagon Office of Strategic Capital loan plus $50M from Commerce (Nov 2025) for a 10,000-tonne rare-earth magnet plant; holds an NdFeB magnet IDIQ (June 2026).

companies.name: Unusual Machines
companies.why: NYSE American-listed (UMAC) drone-parts maker that leased a 17,000 sq ft drone-motor factory in Orlando (June 2025) and has since started US motor production.
companies.note: No USAspending prime awards under 'UNUSUAL MACHINE'.

companies.name: ModalAI
companies.why: US drone flight-computer and autonomy maker ('Open Autonomy for America's Drones'): 9 Army and Navy awards ($6.4M) since 2024, including two Army SBIR Phase IIs.

companies.name: Centrus Energy
companies.why: Its American Centrifuge Operating subsidiary holds $1.41B in DOE awards, including a $900M HALEU enrichment task order (July 2026), and runs the Piketon, OH centrifuge plant licensed under NRC docket 70-7004.
rejected: NAC INTERNATIONAL INC. (UEI Q47MMR9NU144: former USEC subsidiary, still linked under Centrus's parent UEI)
CENTRUS PERSONNEL SOLUTIONS LLC (unrelated staffing firm)
NRC 07007003 (American Centrifuge Lead Cascade Facility, license terminated Nov 2024)

companies.name: Urenco USA (Louisiana Energy Services)
companies.why: Operates a licensed commercial enrichment plant in Eunice, NM (NRC docket 70-3103, 6,000+ filings, safety-analysis updates through Nov 2025) and holds a DOE HALEU enrichment IDIQ (Oct 2024).
rejected: EURENCO BOFORS AB (Swedish explosives maker, substring match on 'URENCO')
URENCO ENRICHMENT CO LTD (UK group parent, one $0 DOE award in 2011; not the US plant)
companies.note: nrc.docket('07003103') exceeds gt/nrc.py's 5,000-document guard (6,020 documents).

companies.name: Orano (Orano Enrichment USA)
companies.why: DOE gave Orano Federal Services a $900M LEU enrichment task order (Apr 2026), and Orano Enrichment USA's license application for an Oak Ridge, TN enrichment plant is under NRC review (docket 70-7038).

companies.name: Global Laser Enrichment
companies.why: Licensing a laser enrichment plant in Paducah, KY, General Matter's own town (NRC docket 70-7033, under review in 2026), with a $28.4M DOE front-end fuel award (June 2026) and a seat on DOE's LEU enrichment IDIQ.
rejected: NRC 07007016 (GE-Hitachi GLE's Wilmington, NC docket, inactive since 2021)

companies.name: Oklo
companies.why: Runs an active NRC licensing project for its Aurora powerhouse (plan updated Sept 2026) plus separate fuel-fabrication and fuel-recycling dockets, and is hiring in Idaho Falls.
companies.note: 05200049 is the 2020 Aurora combined license application the NRC denied in Jan 2022. The USAspending awards under OKLO TECHNOLOGIES, INC. are DOE/ARPA-E agreements whose descriptions name Oklo Inc.

companies.name: Kairos Power
companies.why: Holds NRC construction permits for the Hermes test reactor (Dec 2023) and two Hermes 2 units (Dec 2024) in Oak Ridge, TN; the NRC extended Hermes' construction deadline in 2026.
companies.note: USAspending shows only two small DOE grants (2020) under the Kairos name.

companies.name: X-energy
companies.why: Holds a $921.7M DOE Advanced Reactor Demonstration cooperative agreement (2021) for its Xe-100, and the NRC published an environmental impact statement for its TRISO-X fuel plant in Oak Ridge (Feb 2026).
rejected: NRC 05000614 and 99902117 (Long Mott Generating Station: applicant Long Mott Energy, LLC, a Dow subsidiary)
ATREX ENERGY, INC. (substring match on 'X ENERGY')
companies.note: USAspending spells it 'X ENERGY, LLC'; 'X-ENERGY' with a hyphen returns nothing. TRISO-X files at NRC as Triso-X, LLC but has no USAspending awards under that name.

companies.name: TerraPower
companies.why: The NRC issued the construction permit for Kemmerer Unit 1, its Natrium plant in Wyoming (Mar 2026), and its project company US SFR Owner holds a $1.70B DOE ARDP cooperative agreement.
companies.note: The DOE money sits under US SFR Owner, LLC (the Kemmerer licensee, which also files on TerraPower's docket 99902100), so a 'TERRAPOWER' search finds only $3.0M.

companies.name: Radiant
companies.why: Building factory-made microreactors; its Part 70 license application (NRC docket 70-7045, Tennessee site) is under review with a fee cap set in Sept 2026, and it is hiring in El Segundo, Washington DC and Oak Ridge.

companies.name: Valar Atomics
companies.why: Its Ward 250 reactor reached criticality in Utah under DOE's Reactor Pilot Program (June 2026); raised a $1B Series B led by Sequoia (Aug 2026); the NRC opened a pre-application project for it (Sept 2026).
rejected: VALAR (UEI J72KKAGD8C19: State Department security grantee in Somalia)
VALAR LTD (UEI SD9FLD43QTA5: State Department aviation-security grantee)
NRC 05000616 (Holtec's Palisades SMR-300 docket, surfaced by the Valar search)
companies.note: No USAspending prime awards under the Valar Atomics name.

companies.name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
companies.why: Raised $863M in Aug 2025 (about $3B total, which it says is roughly a third of all private fusion capital) to finish SPARC in Devens, MA and build its first ARC plant in Chesterfield County, VA.

companies.name: TAE Technologies
companies.why: Agreed to an all-stock merger with Trump Media valued at over $6B (Dec 2025), which would make it a listed fusion company; closing was targeted for Q4 2026.
companies.note: No USAspending awards under 'TAE TECHNOLOGIES' or 'TRI ALPHA ENERGY'.

companies.name: Pacific Fusion
companies.why: Launched with $900M of milestone-based Series A commitments (Oct 2024) and broke ground on a roughly $1B pulser research and manufacturing campus in Albuquerque, NM.

companies.name: Figure
companies.why: Valued at $39B after a $1B+ Series C (Sept 2025) to scale its Helix model and BotQ humanoid factory.
rejected: greenhouse:figure (Figure Technology Solutions, a Nasdaq-listed blockchain lender)

companies.name: Skild AI
companies.why: Raised about $1.4B at a $14B+ valuation (Jan 2026; SoftBank-led, NVIDIA participating) for a general robot brain that runs across robot types.

companies.name: Apptronik
companies.why: Closed over $935M of Series A funding with a $520M extension (Feb 2026; Google, Mercedes-Benz and John Deere among backers) to scale its Apollo humanoid, after 14 Army and SOCOM awards ($12.3M).

companies.name: Agility Robotics
companies.why: Its Digit humanoids work in GXO, Schaeffler and Toyota facilities, and it agreed to go public through Churchill Capital Corp XI at a $2.5B valuation (June 2026).

companies.name: Boston Dynamics
companies.why: The legged-robot incumbent: 63 federal awards ($153M) going back to DARPA's LS3 robot mule ($56.7M, 2009) and the Atlas humanoids built for the DARPA Robotics Challenge (2012).

companies.name: Groq
companies.why: NVIDIA struck a reported ~$20B deal (Dec 2025) for a non-exclusive license to Groq's inference-chip technology and hired its founder; Groq stays independent and runs GroqCloud.
companies.note: No USAspending awards under 'GROQ'.

companies.name: Cerebras
companies.why: Listed on Nasdaq (CBRS) in May 2026 in the year's largest US IPO (about $6.4B raised); also sells wafer-scale systems to DOE and the Army.

companies.name: Tenstorrent
companies.why: Raised about $700M at a ~$2.6B valuation (Dec 2024) from Samsung, LG, Fidelity and Bezos Expeditions; hiring for AI silicon in Santa Clara, Austin and Toronto.

companies.name: MatX
companies.why: Raised a $500M Series B (Feb 2026; Jane Street and Situational Awareness leading) to tape out its MatX One LLM chip.
rejected: MATX ENTERPRISES LLC (defense supply vendor in NC and TX)

companies.name: Rocket Lab
companies.why: End-to-end launch and spacecraft company (556 open roles) with $101M in NASA and Space Force awards, including NASA VADR launches and an NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 seat (2025).

companies.name: Impulse Space
companies.why: Orbital-transfer-vehicle maker with 13 Space Force and NASA awards ($63.8M, all since Dec 2023), including a $28.3M SBIR Phase III (2024) and NASA GDC Trailblazer work (Sept 2026).
rejected: ashby:impulse (two generic San Francisco postings, not Impulse Space)

companies.name: Firefly Aerospace
companies.why: NASA lunar-lander and launch contractor: $560M in federal awards, led by Commercial Lunar Payload Services task orders ($117.2M in 2024, $112.8M in 2023), plus Space Force TacRS launches.
companies.note: USAspending files Firefly Space Transport Services under Firefly Aerospace's UEI.

companies.name: Stoke Space
companies.why: Raised a $510M Series D (Oct 2025; about $990M total) to build its fully reusable Nova rocket and Cape Canaveral pad, and holds an NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 seat (2025).

companies.name: Starcloud
companies.why: Flew the first NVIDIA H100 in orbit (Nov 2025), raised $250M at a $2.3B valuation (Aug 2026; $450M total), and is building a 100,000 sq ft satellite factory in Woodinville, WA.
companies.note: No USAspending awards under 'STARCLOUD' or its former name 'LUMEN ORBIT'.

companies.name: Cowboy Space Corporation (formerly Aetherflux)
companies.why: Raised a $275M Series B at a $2B valuation (May 2026, Index Ventures) for orbital data centers built into its own rocket upper stages; renamed from Aetherflux.
companies.note: aetherflux.com now redirects to cowboyspace.com. No USAspending awards under either name.

companies.name: Axiom Space
companies.why: NASA's commercial-station and Artemis spacesuit contractor ($695M in federal awards, incl. $414.5M for xEVAS) and the buyer of the first two on-orbit compute payloads on Kepler's optical relay network (Apr 2025).

companies.name: Herrenknecht
companies.why: German TBM maker behind major US bores, e.g. the $76M custom machine for VTA's BART Silicon Valley extension, bought through Kiewit Shea Traylor.
companies.note: No USAspending awards under 'HERRENKNECHT'.

rejected: ROBBINS COMPANY, THE (UEI Q7P1MF5U1P31: small NASA and DOE vendor in MA and DC, not confirmed as the Ohio TBM maker)

companies.why: Tunnel contractor in the joint ventures boring BART Silicon Valley (Kiewit Shea Traylor) and Seattle's Sound Transit U220 tunnel; its only federal prime awards are two USACE contracts ($42M, 2004-05).

companies.name: Synchron

companies.name: Blackrock Neurotech
companies.why: Long-time neural-interface hardware supplier: its operating company Blackrock Microsystems has 154 federal awards ($22.7M) since 2008, mostly NIH SBIR grants and VA purchases (latest June 2026).
